served.stem: In a three-point testcross, two of the three genes lie 25 centimorgans apart on the chromosome. What recombination frequency is expected between that pair of genes?
served.bankWhy: A centimorgan is defined as one percent recombination, so the conversion is direct and 25 centimorgans corresponds to about 25 percent recombinant offspring. The word approximate matters at larger distances, because a double crossover between two markers restores the parental arrangement and makes the observed frequency read slightly low. That is exactly why a three-point cross, with a marker sitting in the middle, gives better distances than a two-point cross.

answer.line: A centimorgan is defined as 1 percent recombinant offspring, so 25 centimorgans reads straight across as 25%.

steps: Know the definition first: 1 map unit, or centimorgan, is 1 percent recombinant offspring.
Read straight across. 25 centimorgans means about 25% of testcross offspring are recombinant.
Check it against the ceiling. Recombinants never pass 50%, and 25 sits under it.
The third gene changes nothing here.

choices.note: No rule turns 25 map units into 5%. That value fits genes about 5 centimorgans apart, linked far more tightly.
12.5% is one recombinant class. There are two, and together they make 25%.
Map units are percent recombinants, by definition.
50% is what genes show when they assort independently, unlinked or very far apart. These two are linked at 25 map units.
75% is the parental offspring, 100 minus 25. It also sits above the 50% ceiling, so it can never be a recombination frequency.
